Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

before preposition

a time or an event

also before dinner, before dawn, before noon, the year before, prior to, long before

classical

Cic. Att. 12.1.1: ēgrediēns ē vīllā ante lūcem
Sen. Ep. 13.4: nē sīs miser ante tempus
Traupman 278

ante + acc.

preposition with the accusative

Like post, with a time or an event: ante cēnam, ante lūcem, ante merīdiem. For a thing, a clause with antequam. For “ago”, see ago.

Other words

  • annō ante — a year before, the year before

    phrase: ante as an adverb, with the measure of time in the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 19: annō ante mē cēnsōrem mortuus est

    So paucīs ante diēbus, a few days before; paulō ante, a little earlier.

Examples

  • hoc litterulārum exarāvī ēgrediēns ē vīllā ante lūcem

    I scribbled this little note as I left the house before dawnCic. Att. 12.1.1

  • sī volēs in convīviō multum bibere cēnāreque libenter, ante cēnam ēstō crūdam quantum volēs ex acētō

    if you want to drink a lot at a party and enjoy your dinner, eat as much raw cabbage as you like with vinegar before dinnerCato Agr. 156.1

  • nē sīs miser ante tempus

    don’t be unhappy before it is timeSen. Ep. 13.4

  • annō ante mē cēnsōrem mortuus est, novem annīs post meum cōnsulātum

    he died the year before I was censor, nine years after my consulshipCic. Sen. 19

  • atquī tertium, inquit, ante diem scītōte dēcerptam Carthāgine. tam prope ā moerīs habēmus hostem!

    “And yet,” he said, “know that this was picked at Carthage the day before yesterday. So close to our walls is the enemy!”Plin. NH 15.75

  • quam dēlectābat eum dēfectiōnēs sōlis et lūnae multō ante nōbīs praedīcere!

    how he loved to predict eclipses of the sun and moon for us long before!Cic. Sen. 49

  • antelūculō

    before dawnTraupman 300

See also after, ago, before noon, until.
